Report on the Committee's study and decision on the matter of reviewing, among the salaries and allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, the salary and allowances of the Chief Justice

Report No.: M20/R/ML/2026/12
27 October 2026

Finance Committee

The responsibilities of this Committee include checking whether the various expenditures made by State offices are made in the manner permitted by law and in accordance with the budget passed by the Majlis, and checking whether the amounts of money approved by the Majlis are being spent or used for those purposes. They also include the Committee examining, where State offices have spent money beyond the approved amount, the reasons and circumstances that required that money to be spent. In this regard, in looking into matters relating to State finances, they include studying the financial accounts of State offices, State-owned companies, State business enterprises and independent State institutions, studying the various reports of the Auditor General, identifying the measures that must be taken and informing the relevant State offices. In addition, they include carrying out the matters required in relation to the role the Majlis must play in the State taking loans and the State giving guarantees, overseeing the work of the Maldives Monetary Authority and the Auditor General's Office, and seeking the advice of other committees in determining the salaries that must be determined by the People's Majlis.

1. Introduction

As stated in number 10 of Article 120(b) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, the responsibilities of the Finance Committee include advising the Majlis in determining the salaries and allowances that must be determined by the People's Majlis, and seeking the advice of other relevant committees in determining those salaries. Accordingly, this report is the report of the Committee's study and decision on the matter of reviewing, among the salaries and allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, the salary and allowances of the Chief Justice. The schedule included in this report is a part of this report.

2. Documents considered by the Committee in studying the matter

In studying this matter, the Committee considered the following reports.
1. The report passed by the People's Majlis on 28 December 2010, "Report on the Finance Committee's fresh review and decision on the matter, following the Majlis sending back to the Committee the report concluded on 26 August 2010 and submitted to the Majlis by the Finance Committee on reviewing/formulating the salary structure to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution and 10 of Article 100(a) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis";
2. The report passed by the People's Majlis on 31 December 2012, "Report on the Finance Committee's fresh review and decision on the salary structure to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution and 10 of Article 100(a) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis" (Report No. މލކ/2012/ރ-10);
3. The report passed by the People's Majlis on 28 February 2024, "Report on the review and reformulation of the structure of salaries and allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis" (Report No. M19/ML/2024/01).
4. The report passed by the Finance Committee of the People's Majlis on 22 October 2026, "Report on the Committee's study and decision on the matter of reviewing, among the salaries and

[signature] [stamp]

allowances to be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, the salary and allowances of the Speaker of the People's Majlis, the vehicle allowances of members of the Cabinet, and the allowances of island councillors" (Report No. M20/R/ML/2026/11).

3. How the Committee's work proceeded

Among those who receive salaries and allowances that must be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, as the post of Speaker of the People's Majlis and the post of Chief Justice are posts of the same grade, it was decided unanimously by the members present and voting at the Committee's 26th meeting, held on 27 October 2026, that the Finance Committee would take the initiative to review the salary and allowances of the Chief Justice and deliberate on it among the members, in order to equalise the salary of the Speaker of the People's Majlis and the salary of the Chief Justice.

4. How the Committee's deliberations proceeded

At the Committee's 26th meeting, held on 27 October 2026, the members of the Committee deliberated on the following matters.

4.1. Salary and allowances of the Chief Justice

It is noted that the total amount the Chief Justice currently receives as salary and allowances is equal to the salary and allowances received by the Deputy Speaker of the People's Majlis. It is also noted that this salary is less than the salary of the Speaker of the People's Majlis as newly reviewed by the Finance Committee. Accordingly, the Chief Justice currently receives a total of MVR 91,000 (ninety-one thousand) as salary and allowances. After the Committee's fresh review of the salary of the Speaker of the People's Majlis, the Speaker of the People's Majlis will now receive a total of MVR 95,125 (ninety-five thousand one hundred and twenty-five) as salary and allowances. Therefore, in order to arrange for the Chief Justice to receive a salary equal to the salary and allowances of the

[signature] [stamp]

Speaker of the People's Majlis, the Committee decided to review the allowances of the Chief Justice, set MVR 4,125 (four thousand one hundred and twenty-five) as a special allowance, and set a total of MVR 95,125 (ninety-five thousand one hundred and twenty-five) as the salary and allowances of the Chief Justice. With this change, it is estimated that an additional MVR 49,500 (forty-nine thousand five hundred) per year will be spent on the salary and allowances of the Chief Justice compared to what is currently spent. 5. The Committee's decision

Among those who receive salaries and allowances that must be determined by the People's Majlis under Article 102 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, as the post of Speaker of the People's Majlis and the post of Chief Justice are posts of the same grade, after deliberation at the Finance Committee's 26th meeting of 2026 on reviewing the salary and allowances of the Chief Justice in order to equalise the salary of the Speaker of the People's Majlis and the salary of the Chief Justice, the members present at the Committee decided unanimously to set a special allowance for the Chief Justice and to pass it with the change deliberated and reviewed in the Committee.

[signature] [stamp]

The proposed date for providing the salary and allowances with the change proposed to the salary structure by the People's Majlis is from the day this report is passed on the floor of the People's Majlis.

Therefore, we submit this report to the People's Majlis under number 12 of Article 120(b) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, for the Majlis to decide on this report.
